newsitem.title: USA: General Dynamics profits lower for quarter, year.
newsitem.headline: General Dynamics profits lower for quarter, year.

text.p: General Dynamics Corp. said Wednesday its profits for the fourth quarter and all of last year fell from the previous year's levels, which were helped by the disposal of operations.
The big defence contractor said its net income for the three months ended Dec. 31 slipped to $70 million, or $1.11 a share, from $88 million, or $1.40 a share.
For all of 1996, the company said, net income fell to $270 million, or $4.27 a share, from $321 million, or $5.10 a share, in 1995.

The company, based in Falls Church, Va., noted, however, that its 1995 results included income of $55 million from discontinued operations and a $19 million gain from the disposal of those operations.

Excluding those amounts, General Dynammics said, its operating income rose by 10 percent to $70 million from $64 million in the fourth quarter and by 9 percent to $270 million from $247 million for the full year.

The company, which makes warships, submarines, tanks and other weapons systems, said its sales edged up to $896 million from $893 million in the quarter while climbing 17 percent to $3.58 billion from $3.07 billion in the full year.
"This was a strong finish to a year in which we met or exceeded every goal we set for General Dynamics," Chairman and Chief Executive James R. Mellor said in a statement.

"We've continued to reshape the company for the markets we see ahead, making each of our businesses stronger and more competitive. As a result, we've won the programmes we set out to win, made several important acquisitions, improved sales and earnings, and steadily increased our backlog."

The company, which derives almost all its business from U.S. government contracts, said it ended the year with a funded backlog for continuing operations of $6.2 billion and total backlog of $10.4 billion. Comparable amounts last year were $5.2 billion and $7.4 billion, respectively, it said.
General Dynamics' stock added 25 cents to $71.50 in morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
